item.title: Tokyo at New Year: Hatsumode, What's Closed & a Day-by-Day Plan
item.description: New Year (oshogatsu, お正月) is the most important holiday in Japan, and it is the one period when visiting Tokyo is genuinely different from visiting Tokyo at any other time. Not harder — different. The city empties of residents who travel to family homes, trains run half-full, the air is cold and unusually clear, and for a few days the world’s largest metropolis feels almost provincial. Then, at the shrines, the entire country shows up at once.
